query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: seat_comfort_deficiency
per_column.rationale: A candidate cause/actionable lever on the outcome (poor seat comfort depresses rating and recommendation). Query only names the outcome, not seat comfort, so it is a surfaced treatment dimension.

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause of overall rating (attentive vs cold_robotic crew). Not named in query; a treatment lever.

per_column.name: food_beverage_quality_deficiency
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause of the rating; a service-quality treatment dimension, not named in query.

per_column.name: operational_reliability
per_column.rationale: Delays/cancellations/baggage failures are a plausible cause of low rating and non-recommendation; a treatment lever not referenced in the query.

per_column.name: ground_service_failure
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause of the outcome (check-in/gate handling), a treatment dimension surfaced from text.

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause (responsive vs dismissive handling) of dissatisfaction; treatment lever.

per_column.name: service_recovery_adequacy
per_column.rationale: Recovery after a failure is a lever on the outcome. Note it sits partly on a mediating path (failure -> recovery -> outcome) among the other causes, but relative to the focus outcome it is treated as an actionable cause.

per_column.name: communication_failure
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause of dissatisfaction; a treatment dimension, not named in query.

per_column.name: product_quality
per_column.rationale: Cabin/product condition as a candidate cause of the rating; treatment lever.

per_column.name: passenger_segment
per_column.rationale: Type of traveller (solo/couple/family/business) plausibly drives BOTH the service exposure/perception (treatments) and baseline expectations that determine the rating/recommendation. A pre-treatment common cause that must be adjusted for; not named in the query.

per_column.name: service_class
per_column.rationale: Cabin class is upstream of both the service quality actually received (seat/food/crew treatments) and the outcome rating, so it is a genuine common cause requiring adjustment. Not named in the query text.

per_column.name: route_complexity_and_transfer_risk
per_column.rationale: Route/transfer complexity plausibly causes operational_reliability (a treatment) and independently affects the outcome, making it a common cause to adjust for. Not named in query (the 'istanbul' value hints at template contamination but the semantic role is a confounder).

judge.rationale: The set clearly supplies (a) treatments: multiple actionable candidate causes of the overall rating/recommendation (crew service, seat comfort, food, operational reliability, ground service, customer-service responsiveness, recovery, communication, product quality). It also supplies (b) genuine confounders that are pre-treatment common causes of both the service experience and the outcome: service_class (class determines both amenities/service received and satisfaction), passenger_segment (traveller type shapes both exposure and expectations), and route_complexity_and_transfer_risk (drives operational reliability and independently the rating). Crucially, NONE of these confounders are named or clearly implied in the query, which only references the outcome (overall rating / Recommended=no) -- so they were surfaced from the data/text, satisfying the decisive test. Confounder quality is good but not perfect: class is a strong common cause, while segment and route complexity are weaker/somewhat ambiguous (segment could partly reflect self-selection; the stray 'hub_transfer_istanbul_risk' value signals template contamination, and one could argue class/route also act as treatments in places). No column was mislabelled a confounder while actually being a pure mediator or collider. Overall the columns realise the causal-attribution claim.
